query: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperature but a relatively high density of 10.21 g cm−3. What single intervention could reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and at elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000 °C? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict directional changes relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, define the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose an experiment and rejection criterion that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of Hf with additional Zr in the as‐cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy will reduce the overall density without significantly compromising its high strength at room temperature and at elevated temperatures (~1000 °C).
generation.material_initial_state: An as‐cast HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy with a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³ that exhibits high strength at room temperature and up to ~1000 °C.
generation.intervention: Replace a portion (e.g., 25–50%) of the heavy Hf component with extra Zr, thereby increasing the overall Zr content while reducing Hf content.
generation.conditions: Testing in the as-cast state under standard tensile and compressive loading at room temperature and at elevated temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Retention of a single-phase (likely BCC) solid solution layout, with similar lattice distortion characteristics provided by similar atomic radii of Hf and Zr.
generation.mechanism: Since Zr has a lower atomic mass than Hf but has comparable atomic size, its increased proportion in the solid solution is expected to reduce the alloy’s density while preserving the solid-solution strengthening and phase stability that underpin the high strength at both room and elevated temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: A modified alloy with reduced overall density (potentially a reduction of several percent relative to 10.21 g/cm³) while maintaining mechanical properties (yield strength and ductility) within an acceptable range comparable to the original alloy at both room temperature and near 1000 °C.
generation.baseline: The original as-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy, which possesses high mechanical strength and a density of ~10.21 g/cm³.
generation.boundary: Applicable for as-cast alloys tested under standard tensile/compression conditions at temperatures from room temperature up to ~1000 °C; loading conditions should mimic those used for high-temperature applications.
generation.uncertainty: The exact fraction of Hf that can be replaced by Zr without a significant loss in strength is not precisely known. The trade-off between density reduction and retention of high-temperature performance may vary depending on the substitution level and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate three alloy variants: (a) the baseline HfMoTaTiZr, (b) a modified alloy with ~25% of Hf replaced by extra Zr, and (c) a modified alloy with ~50% replacement. Process all alloys under identical as-cast conditions. Conduct standardized tensile and compressive mechanical tests at room temperature and at ~1000 °C, as well as measure the density of each alloy.
measurements: Yield strength and ultimate strength from tensile/compressive tests at room temperature and ~1000 °C
Ductility assessments (elongation, fracture toughness) across the test temperatures
Phase characterization to verify retention of a single-phase BCC structure (XRD/SEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified alloys show either (i) a statistically significant drop in yield strength or ductility (e.g. >15% reduction) relative to the baseline at any test temperature or (ii) no meaningful reduction in density compared to the original ~10.21 g/cm³, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
